t: Find Array Given Subset Sums - Peeling Elements Off the Sorted Sum List
o: We know n and receive all $2^n$ subset sums of a hidden array in scrambled order, and must return any array that reproduces them. The empty subset guarantees 0 is always among the sums, which anchors every step of the recovery. In Example 1 the sorted sums are [-3,-2,-1,0,0,1,2,3]; the smallest adjacent gap is 1, exposing an element of absolute value 1, and pairing every sum s with s+1 splits the list into the subsets without and with that element. Repeating on the half that contains 0 peels off 2, then -3, recovering [1,2,-3]. Example 2 ([0,0,0,0]) shows multiplicities matter: four zeros force the answer [0,0]. With n at most 15 there are at most 32768 sums, so an algorithm making about n halving passes is comfortably fast.
k: The empty subset puts 0 in the sums, and the difference between the two smallest sums equals the absolute value of some hidden element.
Pairing every sum s with s+d splits the list into a lower half L and an upper half L+d; the removed element is +d if we keep L and -d if we keep U - keep whichever half still contains 0.
The greedy pairing is forced at every step because the current minimum cannot pair downward, so each split is unique.
w: Lead with Approach 2; deriving the smallest-gap split demonstrates the key insight, while Approach 1 shows search hygiene. Critical pitfalls: treat sums as a multiset (use counters, not sets); remember the removed element is signed - +d only when the surviving lower half keeps 0, otherwise -d when the shifted upper half does; and never assume the sums are non-negative. Test n = 1 and all-zero inputs. Follow-ups: prove the min-gap lemma formally, or recover the array when only the sorted multiset of sums is streamed.

a.n: Approach 1: Backtracking Over Every Candidate Gap
a.i: A general search view treats any distinct difference between two sums as a candidate absolute value for an element. For each candidate gap d, greedily pair the smallest unconsumed sum s with s+d; a missing partner kills the candidate. A successful pairing yields lower half L and upper half U = L+d: keeping L removes element +d, keeping U removes element -d, and only halves containing 0 are genuine subset-sum families of the remaining elements. Recurse with backtracking until one sum remains.
s: Sort the current multiset of sums and collect all distinct positive gaps between distinct values.
For each gap d, pair each smallest unconsumed s with s+d, consuming both; abort the candidate if any partner is missing.
Form the lower half L and the upper half U = L+d.
Recurse on whichever of L, U contains 0, recording element +d or -d respectively; backtrack on failure.
Stop when a single sum (the empty subset) remains.
a.t: Exponential worst case - every distinct gap is tried with backtracking, far more work than needed once the smallest-gap property is known
a.sp: O(2^n) - each recursion level keeps counters and half-lists sized like its input

a.n: Approach 2: Smallest-Gap Halving With No Search
a.i: Sorting the current sums shows the difference d between the two smallest values always equals the smallest absolute value among the remaining hidden elements: moving from the minimum subset sum to the second minimum requires exactly the cheapest possible membership change. Hence only this one candidate needs testing. The pairing s with s+d is forced (the current minimum cannot pair downward) and always succeeds, producing L and U = L+d; keep the half containing 0 and record +d or -d accordingly. Each pass halves the list, so no backtracking ever fires.
s: Sort the current list; let d be the difference between its two smallest values.
Greedily pair each smallest unconsumed s with s+d; the pairing is forced and succeeds.
Build the lower half L and the upper half U = L+d.
Keep the half that contains 0, recording element +d (kept L) or -d (kept U).
Repeat until one sum remains; the recorded elements are the answer.
a.t: O(2^n * n) - there are n rounds and round k processes about 2^k sums with hashing or sorting
a.sp: O(2^n) - counters and half-lists per round hold at most all remaining sums
